New in 2.0: the command palette (Ctrl+K), workspaces for Explorer, AI Analyst and Pro, a contextual tool pill and a radial menu (tap Space); built-in basemaps and a 3D view when you choose to work online, and an air-gapped file that never uses the network; cloud imagery opened by range from https, S3 and GCS, STAC catalogue search and watched folders; a Convert drop zone for GeoJSON, GeoParquet, FlatGeobuf and Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF of any size; local AI from model packs (SAM 2.1 smart select, Find Objects, Search Imagery, Auto Align, Auto Contrast) and a copilot that uses them first; recipes that run a workflow step by step with review gates; and Send to Photoshop, Illustrator, Blender, Unreal, iOS and Google Sheets. messages.key: GIS Workbench starts on a clean canvas: an app bar on top, a navigation rail on the left (Catalog, Data, Layers, Tools, Measure, AI, Recipes, Convert, Products), one image panel and a small compass at the bottom right of each panel (click it to turn the view north up). Ctrl+K opens the command palette: type a command, a layer, a coordinate or a URL. Hover any button to see what it does. Over an image: tap Space (or press `) for the radial menu; hold F to see the image underneath; hold S for a swipe curtain; Alt + wheel changes the layer opacity; C + drag makes a quick chip for the session deck; Ctrl+V flies to a pasted coordinate; J and K step through markers, detections and search results and 1, 2, 3 triage them. The workspace button in the top bar switches between the Explorer, AI Analyst and Pro set-ups or saves your own. Drag a dock tab to an edge, or onto the lower half of an open dock to see two panels at once; the dock menu collapses a dock to icons. View ▸ Display ▸ Interface Layout (or Preferences ▸ Display) switches to the Classic layout of 1.x and back, without a restart.
